name: API Gateway Pattern
forces_resolved: Single unified entry point for external client applications
Centralizes cross-cutting concerns: authentication, SSL termination, rate limiting, and metrics
Insulates external clients from internal microservice decomposition and address changes
Protocol translation (e.g. external REST/JSON to internal gRPC)
forces_unresolved: Gateway can become a performance bottleneck and single point of failure if not clustered
Risk of business logic creeping into the routing gateway (anti-pattern)
Additional network hop added to all incoming external requests
applicability_conditions: Microservice systems exposed to public internet clients (web, mobile, third-party APIs)
Systems requiring centralized OAuth2 / JWT authentication validation
Architectures needing rate limiting and DDoS protection at the edge
anti_requisites: Simple monolithic applications with direct frontend-backend coupling
Purely internal offline batch data processing systems
Sub-millisecond internal latency requirements where edge proxy hop is unacceptable
